english.title: Sponsor fail to report suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions in another country to the licensing authority

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY THE DETAILS..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 34, 49(1)(i) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
sponsor did not ensure
where a clinical trial was being conducted
at a trial site in another country
in addition to sites in the United Kingdom
all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions
occurring at the site
were reported as soon as possible to the licensing authority
and in any event
in the case fatal or life-threatening reaction, within 7 days beginning with the day after the sponsor was first aware of the reaction OR
in any other case, within 15 days beginning with the day after the sponsor is first aware of the reaction

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 49 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 makes a breach of reg 34 an offence.
(ii) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.
(iii) The legislation was amended as a result of the EU Exit. For offences before 1st January 2021, see H15926.

other.penalty:
Either way - Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
